# MIM repository map for agents

MIM is a Next.js + Electron project. Treat repository state, code and CI as authoritative over stale prose.

## Sources of truth

1. `package.json` — current package version, scripts, dependencies and Electron build configuration.
2. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — checks that actually run in CI.
3. `docs/README.md` — canonical documentation index.
4. `docs/planning/ROADMAP.md` — active technical roadmap.
5. `docs/whosnext.md` — tactical debt / near-term work.
6. `MIM_UNICORN_ENGINEERING_PLAN.md` and `docs/MIM_UNICORN_ENGINEERING_PLAN.md` when present — engineering strategy; verify claims against current code before acting.

Current package version at the time of this map: `11.4.5`.

## Repository layout

- `app/`, `components/`, `lib/` — main application, shared UI and domain logic.
- `web/` — MIMweb / FOMO Hub application and its own TypeScript configuration.
- `standalone/` — Electron desktop shell and packaging helpers.
- `scripts/` — custom test runner, evaluation, benchmarks, release tooling and structural/security checks.
- `docs/architecture/` — system architecture and HTTP API catalog.
- `docs/security/` — threat model, static bytecode security and web hardening docs.
- `docs/engines/` — SAGE, NBT, Aduana and FOMO engine documentation / benchmarks.
- `docs/cloud/` — Supabase/cloud integration documentation.
- `docs/planning/` — roadmap and project-status documents.
- `docs/releases/` — changelog, unreleased notes and release history.
- `docs/adr/` — architecture decision records.

Start documentation discovery at `docs/README.md`; do not guess legacy root-level `docs/*.md` paths when the index points to a themed subdirectory.

## Key technical references

- Architecture master: `docs/architecture/MIM.md`
- Architecture boundaries: `docs/architecture-boundaries.md`
- API catalog: `docs/architecture/API.md`
- Distributed architecture: `docs/architecture/DISTRIBUTED_ARCHITECTURE.md`
- Web hardening: `docs/security/WEB_HARDENING.md`
- SAGE: `docs/engines/SAGE_RESCUE.md`
- SAGE evaluation: `docs/engines/SAGE_EVALUATION.md`
- FOMO: `docs/engines/FOMO_CLOUD.md`
- Roadmap: `docs/planning/ROADMAP.md`
- Project status: `docs/planning/PROJECT_STATUS.md`
- Changelog: `docs/releases/CHANGELOG.md`

## Validation commands

- `npm ci` — reproducible dependency install.
- `npm run lint` — ESLint over `app`, `components` and `lib`. Note: the current script uses `--max-warnings=9999`; warnings are therefore not a failing quality gate.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — root TypeScript verification.
- `npx tsc --project web/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — MIMweb TypeScript verification.
- `npm test` — custom Node/ts-node test runner.
- `npm run test:coverage` — c8 coverage plus the custom test runner.
- `npm run lint:api-guard` — API guard verification.
- `npm run lint:architecture` — architecture boundary verification.
- `npm run build` — Next.js production build.

CI currently runs root/web type checks, lint, API guard, architecture checks/tests, scoped coverage, SAGE contract tests, DAST and a production build in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Testing and coverage boundary

The repository does not use Jest/Vitest/Mocha as its primary runner. Tests are custom scripts orchestrated by `scripts/test-runner.js` and executed with Node/ts-node.

`npm run test:coverage` is intentionally scoped by c8 to:

- `lib/modding/nbt.ts`
- `lib/intelligence/sage/**`

Do not interpret the resulting coverage percentage as whole-repository coverage for UI, cloud, security, Electron or every domain module.

## Electron and secrets

`package.json` currently builds Electron with `asar: false`. This is packaging visibility, not by itself a credential vulnerability in an open-source project.

Desktop API credentials are handled by `standalone/secret-store.js`, which uses Electron `safeStorage`, writes encrypted values to a dedicated secret envelope, uses restrictive file mode `0600` where supported, and migrates supported legacy plaintext settings only after encrypted persistence succeeds. Verify call sites before changing this contract.

## Agent constraints

- Revalidate documentation claims against current `main`, implementation and CI before changing code.
- Prefer one coherent boundary per PR.
- Do not add infrastructure or dependencies only to make the repository look more conventional.
- Do not weaken tests, types, security checks or CI with permissive fallbacks.
- Treat historical release docs and proposals as context, not automatically active requirements.
